name: Abu al-Fadl al-Walid
bio: Ilyas ibn Abdallah Tu'ma, who wrote as Abu al-Fadl al-Walid, was a Lebanese poet of the Arab emigration to the Americas whom al-Zirikli describes as marked by a pure Arab spirit. Born in Qurnat al-Hamra in the Matn in 1886 and educated at the Hikma school in Beirut, he emigrated to South America in 1908 and published a weekly paper, al-Hamra', in Rio de Janeiro, signing himself Abu al-Fadl al-Walid and later al-Walid ibn Tu'ma. He returned home in 1922 and travelled through the Arab lands. His collections include Nafakhat al-Sur, Rayahin al-Arwah, Agharid wa-'Awasif, al-Anfas al-Multahiba and Qasa'id Ibn Tu'ma. He died in 1941.
